newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on looming importer deals.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on looming importer deals.

text.p: The won closed Monday's trading lower against the dollar on looming import account settlements and dealers said many banks took a cautious attitude, fearing a central bank intervention.
Dealers said the dollar would test the 830 won level from the opening bell on Tuesday and added that intervention would decide the market direction.
The won closed at 829.70 after opening at 829.30. It moved in a 829.10-829.80 range.
Dealers said the market failed to test the 830 won level today on a lack of importer deals.

Tuesday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 829.60, the highest level for the dollar since South Korea introduced the market average exchange rate system in 1990. The mid-rate was fixed at 828.70 today.

"Even though the current market position is not large enough to cover importer deals due on Tuesday, the market will move very cautiously on the expectation of intervention by the BOK," said a domestic bank dealer.
Another local bank dealer said the dollar would not fall below the 827 won level tomorrow, even the BOK sells dollars to support the won. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
